page: Google Cloud Platform t2a-standard-2 is an ARM-based general-purpose server instance powered by the Ampere Altra Neoverse-N1 processor. It features 2 dedicated physical cores (2 vCPUs) running at 3.0 GHz with a single thread per core. The hardware configuration includes 8.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and it comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results indicate that the t2a-standard-2 delivers modest performance. Single-core CPU performance via stress-ng is rated as average, and single-threaded gzip compression also performs in the average range. However, multi-core CPU performance and memory bandwidth are relatively weak, with large-block read-only memory bandwidth measured at 26.99 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 16.42 GB/sec. Geekbench scores reflect lower-tier performance, with a single-core score of 1101.0 and a multi-core score of 1997.0. Database operations and Redis SET throughput (2.61 million operations per second) are also positioned in the weaker tier.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the t2a-standard-2 offers a low-cost entry point into the ARM64 ecosystem, making it suitable for developers testing and compiling software for ARM architectures. Given its modest performance profile, it is best suited for lightweight workloads such as basic web serving, development and testing environments, and simple text processing tasks, rather than resource-intensive database operations or heavy multi-threaded computing.
